rationale: The exact candidate asserts first_end and whole_order_end 1906-01-13 and twice says issuance occurred January 13. The complete scanned order on PDF80/printed67 is dated January 12, 1906, signed in print Theodore Roosevelt, and immediately repeals the November 15, 1905 appointment order. There is no delayed-effective clause, condition, administrative implementation period, or evidence of January 13 issuance. The supported direct legal transition is January 12, 1906; the extra day cannot be invented. The correct general distinction between a completed repeal and its surviving legal consequence does not save the exact wrong-date claim. Independently preserved mechanical raw_path_missing defects are an additional unresolved custody-reference limitation, not silently repaired by reading a separately pinned book.
inventory: One operative repeal paragraph, followed by printed signature and White House date; complete source page examined. No independent appointment, removal, reporting, payment, schedule or prospective administration command.
identity: The book prints no EO number. Only IC1911_WPA_LORD_MATCH.csv seq35 and IC1911_ORDERS.csv seq35 used as crosswalks; date January 12, subject repeal of November 15 appointment authority, body and Theodore Roosevelt signature match EO:393. PDF75/printed62 independently reads the November 15, 1905 temporary/permanent appointment authorization, crosswalk seq30 EO:370. Date and subject distinguish the adjacent same-date EO:394; no mere number match.
effective_date_and_first_cessation: The present operative repeal is accomplished by the January 12, 1906 instrument. No earlier cessation of that repeal command can precede its issuance; no evidence supports an additional day. This is a direct legal transition, not inferred real-world performance of a permission or deadline.
savings: No express savings or future duty in this order. The legal cancellation remains its consequence; no claim is made that previous appointments were vacated, employees removed, rights under other instruments extinguished, or appointments ever made. The predecessor permits appointments on predicates; it does not prove their exercise.
earlier_candidates_and_current: No later general revocation is needed as the first completion of this direct repeal. Supplied later-number searches are bounded leads, not exhaustive proof of current law. Rejection does not approve any corrected or unprovided counterpart.
